rv.q: What makes Golyak’s production really roar into flame is the astonishing magnetism of his performers.
Everything about this production is wonderful and it will have you standing and cheering come curtain call.
Golyak and his gifted collaborators sail right down the middle, bringing us something that is two parts slapstick to one part tragedy, seasoned with just enough whimsy and terror.
Golyak’s production achieves delicate balances between timeliness and timelessness, hilarity and horror, and the result is an astonishing piece of work.
Muscular performances and jaw-dropping design come together seamlessly for an evening of theater that will linger in my memory for a long time.
These are the moments that made it worth sitting through a production whose chaos, for all its inventive variation, requires some patience.

What Delirium gets right is capturing the lengths to which people will go to normalize the extreme, the rationalizations of people who've grown accustomed to untenable situations — whether domestic or political.
Igor Golyak is one of the most exciting, inventive, and innovative directors working today, and he proves it yet again with the absolutely mind-blowing Delirium.
For all that is wonderful about this Delirium, the play does not rank among Ionesco's best, and the show's pungency flags.

cn.t: Critics praise Igor Golyak's inventive adaptation of Ionesco's absurdist play, celebrating its timely resonance and the exceptional chemistry between lead actors Chulpan Khamatova and Andrey Burkovskiy in this captivating production.

vr.q: I enjoyed the clever ideas... but it just wasn't working all together for me.
